title: dx-sdk-todo-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for DX SDK docs / sample apps / tutorial fixes. Mostly a running TODO and notes-to-self.

Context:
- Working on the JS/TS SDK quickstart and sample app for the new streaming API and function-calling examples.
- Goals: make onboarding <30min for engineers, include typed client examples, and surface common gotchas (rate limits, retry semantics).

Open tasks (priority ordered):
1) Quickstart README (high)
   - Gap: current README only shows sync generate() call. Need streaming example and function-calling example.
   - Action: add streaming code snippet + note about response chunking and partial JSON assembly.
   - ETA: 2026-03-06 (paired with Mikaela)

2) Sample app: "Chat with Memory" (medium-high)
   - Checklist:
     - [ ] Basic react app scaffold (Vite) with Redwood SDK client init (env var + typed client)
     - [ ] Streaming chat UI (append tokens as they arrive)
     - [ ] Simple local memory (persist to localStorage) + example of prefix caching config
     - [ ] README walkthrough and deploy instructions to Netlify/Vercel.
   - Notes: show how to configure batching vs single-request for low-latency UX.
   - Owner: Evan / Mikaela

3) Tutorial: "Function calling with structured outputs" (medium)
   - Problem: docs show function schema but not how to validate/handle partial responses / errors.
   - TODO: add best-practices section, sample server code to call functions and re-try on invalid JSON.
   - Add small demo that writes results to a typed TS interface.

4) Docs site: code samples consistency audit (low-medium)
   - Issue: some code blocks are JS, others TS; inconsistent import style (require vs import).
   - Action: standardize on TS with minimal JS fallback. Create a lint script or pre-submit check for examples.

5) FAQ + gotchas (low)
   - Add short notes: token accounting for streaming, how KV/prefix caching affects prompts, typical cold-start latencies for small models, and recommended autoscaling knobs for Dedicated.

Notes / fragments:
- Streaming snippet idea (pseudo):
  const stream = client.responses.stream({ model: 'redwood-rt-medium', input: '...'});
  for await (const chunk of stream) { appendToUI(chunk.delta); }
  // mention: handle resume on network errors (resume token)

- Function calling: prefer explicit schemas, validate in worker thread, fall back to text parse when schema validation fails. Suggest a code helper: safeParseFunctionOutput(output, schema) -> {ok, value, errors}.

- Sample app UX notes:
  - Show both optimistic UI (display partial tokens) and a stable final response.
  - Provide toggle to switch model variant and show latency/cost estimate per token.

Unresolved questions / design decisions:
- Should sample apps include Redwood Console screenshots or a mock console? (ask Product: Mikaela)
- How much infra setup should the tutorial handle (Vercel deploy automated, or manual env var config)? Lean towards automated deploy + note about secrets.

Short-term schedule (this sprint):
- Week 1 (by 2026-03-06): Quickstart README streaming + function calling snippets; start chat sample scaffold.
- Week 2 (by 2026-03-13): Finish sample app features, write tutorial for function calling, add CI checks for code sample style.

Links to reference artifacts (to add into final docs):
- internal: CONFLUENCE-DR-4567 (streaming API spec)
- GH repo drafts: GH-PR-1289 (sample app scaffold)
- Jira doc ticket: JIRA-DOC-3421

Quick personal notes:
- Keep examples minimal—focus on 1 clear path from zero -> deployed.
- Avoid deep infra; include links to Dedicated docs for enterprise setup.
- Remind SRE/infra to review the sample app's recommended concurrency settings.

Next immediate actions (today):
- Write streaming README snippet and push branch (evan/dx/streaming-snippet).
- Ping Mikaela about sample-app UI design (slack thread: #dx-sample-app).

TODO (one-line):
- [ ] README streaming snippet
- [ ] function-calling tutorial draft
- [ ] chat sample scaffold PR
- [ ] types + helper: safeParseFunctionOutput
- [ ] code sample style lint

End of scratchpad.
